title: In 1996, a film crew ate Clam Chowder laced with PCP. I made a game about it.
author: katatonicmango
selftext:
Playable free in the browser: [https://kedikatstudios.itch.io/royal-flush](https://kedikatstudios.itch.io/royal-flush)

The inspiration behind the game: [https://variety.com/2022/film/news/titanic-crew-members-drugged-pcp-clam-chowder-1235465618/](https://variety.com/2022/film/news/titanic-crew-members-drugged-pcp-clam-chowder-1235465618/)

This game was originally meant for a mobile submission for Epic's MegaJam, but we ran out of time. I'm quite proud of it anyway and would love to hear your thoughts!

  
Some stats:

\- About 15 hours from empty folder to public [itch.io](http://itch.io) page

\- 49 prompts from me. Roughly a third were just "yes, upload it"

\- 1,151 tool calls by the agent, 32 commits

\- 6,197 lines of JavaScript (Three.js + GSAP), none typed by me

\- 0 image or audio assets. Every texture is drawn on a canvas in code: the PS1 dithering, vertex wobble and 240p render are shaders, and the music is synthesized live including a public-domain hymn for level 3 (The song the band played as the ship was going down in the movie!)

\- \~706k output tokens; \~278M tokens read, 99% of that cached context



Things that worked:

\- Keeping one quality bar written down: "AAA game feel in a PS1 graphics package." Whenever something felt stiff (blocky shoulders, poses snapping), I pointed back to it, and the fix applied across every level.

\- Having it build a headless autoplay bot early. Every level change was checked by the bot playing through it, which caught impossible obstacle layouts before I did. 

\- Giving feedback with reference images instead of adjectives. "Make the comics look like 1996 low-poly games" plus three screenshots beat any amount of describing.



Things that didn't:

\- The first comic cutscenes looked amateurish and had to be rebuilt as 3D renders.

\- Physics on the tilted level 3 took several rounds before objects slid in a way that felt fair.



Happy to answer questions about the workflow!
